question: What temporal limits apply in the month of Māgha within the recurring monthly observance?
premises: The month of Māgha is specifically designated.
The observance may extend up to the sixth lunar day.
The observance may extend up to the festival juncture in every month.
inference: In the month of Māgha, the observance is delimited by the sixth lunar day or by the festival juncture, in accordance with the rule for every month.
uncertainties: Whether ṣaṣṭhyantaṃ and parvāntaṃ are alternative or cumulative limits is not explicit.
plain_english: In the month of Māgha, the observance extends up to the sixth day or up to the festival juncture, as it does in every month.
